objective: Establish a fail-closed staging-to-canonical reconciliation audit that prevents stale or divergent staging candidates from being promoted and records exact staging configuration drift without changing production or backend credentials.
productionBaselineEvidence: verified: Android Production OTA run #249 published update 01a1a62f-f53e-7569-a4ef-306df0e0082b on production channel, Android runtime 1.3.2, from source SHA 4ed0d427b54c9ced99dfc0615b19f8cfac8dabab. Current main includes later non-OTA source changes; this audit does not assert current main is the live installed production artifact.
chosenApproach: Add a read-only Git ancestry gate, a manually invoked exact-ref GitHub Actions audit, focused Node tests, and a reconciliation runbook. Keep the old staging branches untouched and create a clean source candidate from canonical main.
selectionRationale: The staging candidates are independently confirmed to be behind and diverged from main. Whole-merging them risks rolling back current UI, branding, media and other product changes. A read-only gate plus clean baseline candidate blocks regression while preserving unique commits for individual review.
preserveBehaviors: Production source, OTA channel, installed clients, Supabase data and credentials remain unchanged
Existing staging-only commits remain available for selective forward-port review
Staging must contain canonical main ancestry before promotion
A green ancestry gate never bypasses regression, runtime/channel compatibility, RC or visible verification
acceptanceChecks: A staging candidate behind main is blocked
A diverged staging candidate is blocked even when it contains unique commits
A candidate containing all canonical main history is reported as ancestry-ready but still requires release gates
Invalid commit counts and unprovable Git ancestry fail closed
The audit does not run merge, reset, rebase, build, OTA or production deployment commands
alternativeApproaches: Whole-merge the old staging-user branch into main (rejected: it is diverged and behind, so it risks rolling back newer canonical changes)
Force-reset the existing staging branch to main (rejected: it destroys or obscures staging-only commit history and does not prove installed-client backend compatibility)
Publish current main immediately to the staging-user channel (rejected: the exact installed staging EAS environment, runtime and backend target have not been verified)
